findings.title: $__range queries are split after interpolation removes the guard
findings.body: runSplitQuery now runs datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. Grafana puts __range, __range_s, and __range_ms on request.scopedVars from the full dashboard/Explore range, and applyTemplateVariables sends the expression through templateSrv.replace, so those tokens are already gone when isQueryWithRangeVariable runs. The guard therefore never matches, and queries that the comment says must not be split are partitioned into day-sized chunks. Previously the raw expression still contained $__range, so the query was one request and the backend interpolated the macro against the original range. After this change a common metric such as rate({app="foo"}[$__range]) over 30 days becomes rate({app="foo"}[30d]) executed as ~30 one-day requests, each with a 30-day lookback. That multiplies bytes scanned by roughly the chunk count and turns queries that used to succeed into timeouts, limit errors, or aborted splits (shouldStop on the first failed chunk). Decide splitting from the original expression, keep $__range queries in the non-splitting group (they can still be interpolated so other variables resolve), and add a test that such a query calls runQuery once.

findings.title: $__auto is still expanded per chunk; the new test stubs it away
findings.body: The early interpolation only calls applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) and does not inject an __auto value. $__auto is not a Grafana scoped macro ($__interval and $__range are); this file already notes that step handling lives in the backend (pkg/tsdb/loki/step.go) and is only replicated here for chunk boundaries. applyTemplateVariables also cannot compute it: that API receives no time range or intervalMs. Split sub-requests therefore still contain literal $__auto, and the backend substitutes a step derived from each chunk's shorter range, so chunks get different range vectors and the merged series do not match an unsplit query. The new "Interpolates queries before execution" test hides this by replacing templateSrv.replace with a function that unconditionally rewrites $__auto to 5m, which production replace will not do. Substitute $__auto from the original request range (using the same calculateStep result used to partition) before splitting, and assert the executed expression without stubbing that replacement.

findings.title: Shard path applies template variables twice, duplicating ad-hoc filters
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target with applyTemplateVariables, then splitQueriesByStreamShard always executes those targets through runSplitQuery, which applies applyTemplateVariables again after interpolateShardingSelector has rewritten the LogQL to inject __stream_shard__. For one target and four shard groups that is five substitutions; the updated test locks this in by expecting applyTemplateVariables toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5), where it previously expected a single interpolateVariablesInQueries call. The second call is not a no-op: it is passed request.filters again, so ad-hoc matchers are inserted into an expression that already has them, and the executed query looks like {app="foo", env="prod", __stream_shard__=~"1|2", env="prod"}. A second templateSrv.replace pass can also rewrite $... text that the first substitution or the shard rewrite introduced. Interpolate once, before shard grouping and selector lookup, and skip the new interpolation inside runSplitQuery when the caller already did it.

findings.title: Blank expressions are no longer dropped after interpolation
findings.body: The empty-expression filter now runs on the raw target, before applyTemplateVariables. The previous shard path interpolated with interpolateVariablesInQueries and only then dropped falsy expr values. A target whose expression is only a variable, such as expr "$logql" resolving to "", used to be removed and is now kept, grouped, and sent to Loki. The parse error is not retriable, so the shard loop sets shouldStop and never runs the remaining groups — one blank interpolated target fails every other query in the request. The same order was introduced in runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts filters on query.expr and only then maps applyTemplateVariables), with the same abort-the-batch consequence. Filter hidden targets, interpolate, then drop targets whose expression is blank.
